The short answer

Taxi Saudi Arabia arranges pre-booked private cars to, from and around Taif through a vetted partner network. Taif, practically

What to know before you travel to Taif

Taif sits high on the Sarawat escarpment above Makkah, so the road there and the weather on arrival are different from the coast.

Al Hada or Al Sail road?

From Makkah the car climbs either the Al Hada road — steep hairpin bends with wide views — or the longer, gentler Al Sail road through As-Sail Al-Kabir. Families with children or older passengers often prefer Al Sail; say which you want. If Al Hada is closed for works, the driver uses Al Sail.

Non-Muslim travellers

Non-Muslims cannot enter Makkah under Saudi law. From Jeddah or Jeddah Airport the driver takes the signed road that bypasses the city, so tell us when you book and the route and timing are planned around it.

Jeddah to Taif route details

Umrah from Taif

Qarn al-Manazil at As-Sail Al-Kabir is the Miqat on the Taif side. If you are heading to Makkah for Umrah, ask for a stop when you book — whether it applies to you is your own decision.

Miqat locations guide

Al Hada, Al Shafa and the city

Al Hada is on the mountain road towards Makkah; Al Shafa is the high country south of the city with farms and resorts. Give us the resort or farm name — they are spread out and not next to each other.

Cooler, and busy in summer

Taif is much cooler than Makkah, Jeddah or Riyadh, which makes it a summer escape. Weekends and summer holidays are the busiest times on the roads, so book early.

Looking for car rental?

We do not rent self-drive cars — every booking is a car with a professional driver. If you would rather not drive the mountain roads yourself, a pre-booked car with a driver is the alternative.

Plan your timing

What changes timing on the way to Taif

01

The mountain climb

Al Hada is slow and winding; Al Sail is longer but gentler. Either way the last part is slower than a motorway.

02

Summer weekends

Weekend traffic between Makkah, Jeddah and Taif is heavier in summer. Leave earlier in the day.

03

Spring rose season

The rose harvest in spring is a busy time to visit the farms — book the day trip early.

04

Long legs from Riyadh and Madinah

Riyadh is about 785 km and Madinah about 480 km — plan most of a day, with prayer and rest stops.

FAQ

Taif transport questions

Ask on WhatsApp

How do I get from Makkah to Taif?

By road, about 90 km — roughly ~1 hr 10 min up the Al Hada road or the gentler Al Sail road. A private car collects you from your Makkah hotel and drops you at your Taif address, with the fare agreed before booking.

How far is Taif from Jeddah?

About 170 km by road, roughly ~2 hr. From Jeddah Airport it is about 180 km. Non-Muslim passengers are driven on the road that bypasses Makkah.

Can I book a day trip to Taif from Makkah or Jeddah?

Yes. Book a timed return, or a driver by the hour so the car waits at Al Hada, Al Shafa and the rose farms. The day is quoted as one fare before you travel.

Which car is best for the Taif mountain road?

A sedan suits one to three people with normal luggage. Families usually choose a full-size SUV such as a GMC Yukon XL, and larger groups a Hyundai Staria or a Hiace. We confirm the vehicle against your passengers and bags.

Is this car rental at Taif airport?

We do not rent self-drive cars — every booking is a car with a professional driver. We meet you at arrivals at Taif Regional Airport (TIF) and drive you where you need to go.

Can the driver stop at the Miqat on the way to Makkah?

Yes, if you ask when you book. Qarn al-Manazil at As-Sail Al-Kabir is the Miqat on the Taif side; whether a stop applies to you is your own decision.

Can my company or group be invoiced?

Yes. Email an RFQ for a written quote. Corporate invoicing can be arranged through our sister company.

Is transport in Taif available 24/7?

Yes. Pre-book early-morning and late-night trips so the car and driver are planned in advance. Free cancellation up to 24 hours before pickup.
